key_insight: Identity-paired progressive depth training keeps new VQA layers initialized to the identity, avoiding initialization shock while still improving optimization through added local rotation capacity after expressibility saturates.
engineering_relevance: For hardware-efficient quantum circuits, this offers a cheaper and more stable training curriculum that reduces CNOT overhead and can make deeper variational ansätze easier to optimize in practice.
method: Train a shallow variational circuit first, then append forward/inverse block pairs that cancel to identity at initialization.
Use a single entangling layer plus overparameterized single-qubit rotations so depth increases mainly expand local parameterization, not entangling cost.
Apply a continuation-style acceptance rule to guarantee monotone energy improvement during progressive training.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a theoretical reachable-set saturation result, monotone energy guarantees, fidelity-error bounds via spectral gaps, and a resource analysis showing lower total gate cost than baseline methods.
watch_item: The benefits rely on the identity-pair construction and a single effective entangling layer, so performance may be sensitive to ansatz design, hardware constraints, and whether the accepted continuation steps avoid poor local minima.
paper_title: Identity-Paired Progressive Depth Training: When Trainability Persists Beyond Expressibility
